name: Hulda Brack
role: Head of the machine shop — every one of the party's repair crews answers to her
designNotes:
Created 2026-09-20 at Ingram's direct request for an ally: 'we want to bring allies to the group so that they aren't thinking that they work in a nightmare of an organisation... make them female please. Make them non-human, but not an alien or mitflit.' Characterisation given directly on the follow-up: 'a big tough love, huge energy strong woman with arms like girders and a personality to match. She's in charge of all the players repair crews so she's an important person to be on the right side of, she's friendly, she's no-nonsense and as you said she wants her frames and vehicles undamaged along with the pilots where possible.'

WHY NUAR: it is in data/campaign/ancestry-catalogue.json, so it is real in this setting rather than invented. It was first picked as Golarion-native, to fit the brief's "not an alien"; LEDGER #39 made nuar an alien people, and LEDGER #44 keeps her one: she is a nuar, and alien (the 2026-09-27 note below). Tengu was considered first for the Shōwa setting and rejected on checking; it is not in the catalogue. NOTE: the catalogue's stock flavour text for Nuar references 'home and history lost to the vacuum of the Gap'. DISREGARD THAT — the Gap is a FUTURE event in this campaign, not a past one (Ingram, 2026-09-20), and that text is inherited SF2E filler. Brack's history is her own and is open; it has nothing to do with the Gap.

STRUCTURAL JOB 1 — she is the face of the request-fulfilment loop. Ingram's 2026-09-20 design has players messaging their ground crew for what they want, with Claude reading those requests out of scraped Foundry logs and answering with balanced options (open-questions.json#levelling-and-request-fulfilment). That loop needed a named person on the other end; she is it. The six repair-chief placeholders (repair-chief-*.json) report to her, which turns that layer into something real rather than six unconnected stubs.

STRUCTURAL JOB 2 — she is the Section Officer's exact inverse. He uses the Directorate's machinery against the party; she uses the same machinery for them, and knows precisely which forms matter and which do not. Same institution, opposite direction. She cannot protect them from him and will say so plainly rather than promise otherwise.

APPEARANCES: first seen at the Assembly in Episode One (episode-c1e1--assembly) as one of the department heads on the platform — loud enough to be noticed, not yet spoken to. First real contact is Episode Two's Familiarisation, where she runs the hangar and hands out the machines. Exact age, history before the Directorate, and what she did before this floor are all open.

2026-09-27 (Ingram, LEDGER #44): she is alien after all, overriding this brief's "not an alien". Ingram: aliens are treated as outsiders in this Japan in Golarion, and disguise magic is so freely available that glamoured clothing can be bought on the high street. Hulda says "Fuck that..." and refuses to disguise or moderate her appearance for anyone, as many other aliens in the city do. She draws little attention on the base and a lot more in the city. (The Casebook's version 7 had first made her a minotaur to keep her Golarion's own; overturned.)
status: named and conceived — voice and history still open

facts.text: She calls people by the machine they are standing next to until they have earned a name, and she remembers precisely when each of them did.

revealTrigger.narrative: Being in her workshop for ten minutes and listening to how she addresses anybody.

facts.text: Nothing leaves her floor that she has not signed off, and she has refused officers to their faces. If she says a machine is not going out, it is not going out, and rank does not move her.
Admitting you are useless with your hands gets more of her attention, not less. It is the people who tell her they are handy that she watches.

revealTrigger.narrative: Being honest with her once about not knowing how to do something.
